messages:
maya: Noticing a spike in east-2 GPU pod-to-pod latency and intermittent packet drops since last night's Calico bump to 3.29.0. Training jobs failing NCCL allreduce intermittently.

sam: ugh. saw the same on a couple of nodes — p99 jumps from ~7ms to 120-300ms and then recovery. any packet loss in dmesg?

eli: I grabbed tcpdump and a quick `rdma pingpong` from the affected pods. There's reordering and large segments being split oddly. Looks like large frames from VF -> host are being fragmented.

maya: calico upgrade notes mention changes to encapsulation offload handling for Geneve. our GPU nodes use SR-IOV VFs for intra-rack traffic and RDMA between pods. could be MTU/offload mismatch.

sam: ran `ethtool -k` on a VF and a PF: GRO/TSO/SG were enabled on VF but offload behavior differs after the calico daemonset change. toggling GRO on the VF temporarily dropped reordering.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: calico/3.29.0 rollout -> canary completed on east-2-azb at 03:12 UTC, then staged cluster-wide at 03:40 UTC.

jordan: timeline matches: first NCCL retries at 03:55. We should isolate before rolling back cluster-wide.

eli: quick repro steps I did:
```
# on a GPU node with VF
iperf3 -s -B <vf-ip> &
# from a pod bound to a different VF
iperf3 -c <vf-ip> -P 8 -t 30
# observe reordering in wireshark/tcpdump
```

eli: disabling GRO on the VF fixed the reordering in the test (switching to `ethtool -K <vf> gro off`). That also dropped throughput but stabilized latency.

maya: so likely calico's Geneve/GSO/GRO handling + SR-IOV offload path interaction. Any config knob in calico to bypass offload tweaks?

sam: there is `felix.features` and some encapsulation offload toggles in the v3.29 changelog. Also `CALICO_DISABLE_INTERNODE_ENCAPSULATION` in our helm values was left default.

jordan: immediate mitigation options: 1) Roll back calico to previous patch on east-2 (safer but slow), 2) Disable GRO/TSO on VFs via daemonset (fast but throughput hit), 3) Patch calico DaemonSet to force host NIC offload compatibility flag if present.

maya: cost/operational note: disabling offloads on all GPU VFs will reduce throughput and increase job runtime -> higher cloud GPU hours and cost. We should only apply to affected AZs/nodes.

sam: proposal: create a targeted DS that runs `ethtool -K <vf> gro off tso off` for nodes labelled `gpu-east2` and add a taint to repel scheduling during the apply window. Test for 1 hour. If stable, escalate to partial rollback plan.

eli: I'll prepare the DS and a capture job to run training smoke tests. Also will open a calico issue with our captures + `ethtool` outputs.

jordan: I'll coordinate with oncall to gate any autoscaler activity and make sure we don't spin new GPU nodes into the bad pool.

maya: thanks. please paste DS YAML here when ready and the exact node selector. also include rollback steps. :thumbsup:

sam: DS YAML ready in the ticket, node selector `k8s.node/gpu=true,gce_zone=east2-b`. patch applied to canary 2 nodes now. monitoring looks better.

eli: can reproduce: latency p99 back to ~9-15ms, NCCL job succeeded for the canary nodes. Captures uploaded to the calico ticket.

maya: good work. next actions: 1) expand DS to affected AZs, 2) open an incident postmortem entry (latency + cost impact), 3) coordinate rollback if calico team confirms a config fix.

ops-bot: incident-bot: incident created #INC-2026-112: calico 3.29 SR-IOV/GRO regression east-2 GPU nodes.

sam: adding cost estimate: if we disable offloads cluster-wide for GPUs for 24h, expect ~12-18% runtime increase on large trainings -> ~+$30k over 24h across active runs. I'll add that to the incident ticket.

maya: noted. keep updates in the incident thread. closing thread here but will follow on the incident and calico ticket.
